case_title: Satishchandra Ratanshah v. State of Gujarat and Another
neutral_facts: The accused, a retired bank employee, approached a money lending company for a loan of Rs. 27,00,000/- and received the funds, which were to be repaid within a year with interest. The accused did not repay the loan, and the complainant, who was the director of the company, alleged that the accused had threatened him with dire consequences. Based on these allegations, the complainant filed an FIR against the accused under various sections of the IPC. A charge sheet was filed against the accused under sections 406, 420, and 417 of the IPC. The accused filed an application seeking quashing of the FIR and charges. A summary civil suit was also filed by the complainant to recover the loan amount, which is still pending. The High Court dismissed the quashing petition and directed the trial court to complete the trial. The Supreme Court quashed the proceedings initiated based on the FIR, finding that the allegations were civil in nature and did not constitute a criminal offense.
